items.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was hanging with a bunch of people that hung in the Village at that particular time too: Virginia Cox, the artist

ctx.x: Yeah. Harvey was somebody that was a painter that I knew back when I – before, like 1947, ’48. I was hanging with a bunch of people that hung in the Village at that particular time too: Virginia Cox, the artist, and Harvey Cropper and a bunch of young poets and painters and musicians and stuff. We thought we had a scene, reading those books about the Village and Paris in the ’20s and all like that. It was exciting to try to be a part of something like that. A lot of talent there too.
How active was your reading life at this time?
